svg.aria-label: How to write 钱: 10 strokes · 9 pen lifts · 10 movements
svg.title: Writing 钱
svg.desc: 10 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 钱 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 钱.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E9%92%B1.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 钱, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw the metal piece 钅 on the left: a left-falling stroke, two short horizontals, a short bar rising to the right, then a vertical that flicks up to the right at its foot without lifting. Medians 6–10 draw the right side: two short horizontals, a long slanting stroke that hooks up at its foot without lifting, a left-falling stroke across it, then a dot at the top right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto draws 钅's first stroke shorter than the source's and its fourth stroke level, where the source's rises to the right.
